subtype: Approach: leaving it to the last week [Pitfall]
passage:
On the first day of term, the Class 9 team in the Andheri school got their assignment: a solar cooker model, due in six weeks. Dolma, the leader, said, "Six weeks is forever. Let's meet once and plan." They met once, in the second week, drew a sketch and went home.

Nobody met again. There was always another test.

In the final week, Dolma called everyone to her flat. Farida came. Two others didn't: one had a fever, and one was at a family wedding in Nashik.

Dolma and Farida worked late on two evenings with cardboard and foil. The reflector kept slipping. They taped it at a strange angle. On the day, the teacher tested it in the sun and it barely warmed the water.

Farida said quietly on the way out, "We had six weeks, Dolma."

qa.q: How long did the team have for the solar cooker?
What was Farida feeling when she said "We had six weeks, Dolma"?
qa.a: Farida felt frustrated and disappointed, perhaps a little resentful about the rushed final evenings.

qa.q: What else could the team have tried in the first week?
qa.a: They could have set weekly mini-deadlines, like the reflector done by week three, so two absences at the end would not sink the model.

qa.q: How might the teacher have seen the model that barely warmed the water?
qa.a: The teacher probably saw a rushed job with obvious flaws and may have wondered why a six-week task looked like it was done in two evenings.

grounding: Shows a group assuming there is plenty of time, meeting once, then finishing in a rush with absent members and an obviously flawed model.

subtype: Approach: leaving it to the last week [Pitfall]

"Hafsa, the project's due Monday," Keerthana said, standing by the lockers. "The irrigation model. We haven't touched it."

"We met in July! We made the plan."

"And then nothing. Mehr's in Chennai for her grandmother's surgery. Ravi's got typhoid."

Hafsa leaned on the locker. "I thought we had so much time."

"Everyone thought that."

"Okay. My place, Saturday. Bring whatever pipes you have."

On Saturday the two of them worked six hours. The channels leaked. The little pump from Keerthana's old fish tank didn't fit the pipe. They wrapped it in tape.

On Monday Mr. Pillai poured water into it. It dribbled onto the table.

"What happened?" he asked.

Hafsa looked at the puddle. "We left it to the last week, sir."

"I can see that."

qa.q: What did Keerthana use for the pump?
qa.a: The pump came from Keerthana's old fish tank.

qa.q: How did Hafsa feel when admitting they had left it to the last week?
qa.a: Hafsa felt embarrassed and regretful, staring at the puddle instead of the teacher.

qa.q: What would have helped more than one July meeting?
qa.a: A fixed short meeting every week with small goals would have kept the model moving, so two absences at the end would not matter as much.

qa.q: How might Mehr and Ravi feel when they return and see the grade?
qa.a: They might feel guilty and left out, even though illness and a family emergency were not their fault, since the plan relied on everyone being there at the end.

grounding: Shows a group that met only once and left the work to the last week, then finished in a rush with absent members and a flawed model.
